--- title: "Cholesterol's link to death looks different at different ages" subtitle: "Each tile compares the death rate of US adults in one cholesterol group with adults at 180–199 mg/dL (1.00). 1.27 means a 27% higher death rate; 0.80 means 20% lower." description: "US adults with total cholesterol of 240+ mg/dL had a 27% higher death rate than those at 180–199, but that excess was no longer detectable after taking age and sex into account, and the pattern differed by age group. Survey-weighted Cox models on NHANES 1999–2018 linked to mortality through 2019. Built in R with ggplot2, ggtext, survival and survey." date: "2026-11-16" author: - name: "Steven Ponce" url: "https://stevenponce.netlify.app" citation: url: "https://stevenponce.netlify.app/data_visualizations/TidyTuesday/2026/tt_2026_46.html" categories: ["TidyTuesday", "2026"] tags: [ "TidyTuesday", "Public Health", "Cholesterol", "Mortality", "NHANES", "Survival Analysis", "Cox Regression", "Survey Weights", "Hazard Ratios", "Age Adjustment", "Tile Matrix", "ggtext", "survey", "2026" ] image: "thumbnails/tt_2026_46.png" format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 5 code-link: true code-fold: true code-tools: true code-summary: "Show code" editor_options: chunk_output_type: inline execute: freeze: true cache: true error: false message: false warning: false eval: true --- ![Tile matrix titled Cholesterol's link to death looks different at different ages. Each tile compares the death rate of US adults in one total cholesterol group with adults at 180 to 199 mg/dL, set at 1.00. Before taking age and sex into account, adults at 240+ mg/dL had a 27% higher death rate (1.27); after, the estimate was 1.00, showing no clear difference. Within age groups, the 240+ estimate was 1.42 for ages 18 to 49 (based on 128 deaths and sensitive to survey weighting), 1.02 for ages 50 to 69, and 0.91 for ages 70 and over. Below 160 mg/dL, death rates were higher in every row, from 1.19 to 1.46; treatment and underlying illness were not measured. Average age rose from 42 in the lowest cholesterol group to 51 in the highest. Data: NHANES 1999 to 2018 linked to NCHS mortality records through 2019.](tt_2026_46.png){#fig-1} ::: {.key-takeaways} [Key takeaways]{.key-takeaways-label} - The higher mortality hazard associated with total cholesterol of 240+ mg/dL was no longer detectable after accounting for age and sex. Adults in that cholesterol group were older on average (51 years versus 46 in the comparison group). - In survey-weighted Cox models of 52,634 adults and 7,632 deaths, the estimated hazard ratio at 240+ mg/dL changed from 1.27 (95% CI: 1.14–1.40) before adjustment to 1.00 (0.90–1.11) afterward. The cholesterol–mortality association differed across age groups (interaction p = 0.00025), while cholesterol below 160 mg/dL was associated with higher mortality hazard in all three age groups, relative to 180–199 mg/dL. - Individual cholesterol-group comparisons are exploratory and were not adjusted for multiple testing. The 18–49 estimate at 240+ mg/dL is sensitive to survey weighting, and the data lack statin use, smoking, and baseline illness information. These associations do not establish cause and effect. ::: ### [**Steps to Create this Graphic**]{.mark} #### [1. READ IN THE DATA ---- ## Read every field as character with no NA tokens; restore numbers column by column. read_chr <- function(path) { read_csv(path, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character(), show_col_types = FALSE) } tt_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-11-17/" cm_raw <- read_chr(paste0(tt_url, "cholesterol_mortality.csv")) est_raw <- read_chr(here::here("data/TidyTuesday/2026/tt_2026_46_estimates.csv")) ``` ```` ::: #### [3. Tidy Data]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: tidy #| warning: false ### |- analysis population ---- cm <- cm_raw |> mutate(across(c(total_chol, hdl, died), \(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(na_if(x, "NA"))))) an <- cm |> filter(!is.na(total_chol), !is.na(hdl), hdl <= 140) n_adults <- nrow(an) n_deaths <- sum(an$died) ### |- estimates ---- bins_raw <- c("<160", "160-179", "180-199", "200-219", "220-239", "240+") bins_show <- c("Below 160", "160–179", "180–199", "200–219", "220–239", "240+") est <- est_raw |> mutate( across(c(value, lo, hi, deaths), \(x) as.numeric(na_if(x, ""))), col = match(bin, bins_raw) ) hr <- est |> filter(kind == "hr_weighted") ### |- matrix layout: rows top to bottom = the reading order ---- ## groups (1), (2), (3) are separated by wider gaps than rows within a group, so the ## matrix reads as three steps, not one heatmap row_y <- c(crude_all = 6.3, adj_all = 4.95, adj_18_49 = 3.3, adj_50_69 = 2.3, adj_70p = 1.3) cells <- hr |> mutate( y = unname(row_y[row_key]), status = case_when( bin == "180-199" ~ "ref", lo > 1 ~ "higher", hi < 1 ~ "lower", TRUE ~ "unclear" ), lab_hr = if_else(status == "ref", "1.00", sprintf("%.2f", value)), lab_ci = case_when( status == "ref" & row_key == "crude_all" ~ "comparison", status == "ref" ~ "", TRUE ~ sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", lo, hi) ), y_hr = if_else(lab_ci == "", y, y + 0.13) ) ### |- numbers quoted in copy (all from the export) ---- pick <- function(key, b, k = "hr_weighted") est |> filter(kind == k, row_key == key, bin == b) crude_240 <- pick("crude_all", "240+") adj_240 <- pick("adj_all", "240+") young_240 <- pick("adj_18_49", "240+") young_unw <- pick("adj_18_49", "240+", "hr_unweighted") mean_age <- est |> filter(kind == "mean_age_weighted") |> arrange(col) pct_crude <- round((crude_240$value - 1) * 100) dip <- pick("adj_50_69", "200-219") pct_dip <- round((1 - dip$value) * 100) age_240 <- mean_age$value[mean_age$bin == "240+"] age_ref <- mean_age$value[mean_age$bin == "180-199"] ``` ```` ::: #### [5. Visualization Parameters]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: params #| include: true #| warning: false ### |- plot aesthetics ---- clrs <- get_theme_colors( palette = list( higher = "#9A4A2E", lower = "#4D6478", unclear = "#E6DFD3", ref = "#FFFFFF", ink = "#2C2825", muted = "#7A7068", outline = "#7A7068" ) ) col_higher <- clrs$palette$higher col_lower <- clrs$palette$lower col_unclear <- clrs$palette$unclear col_ref <- clrs$palette$ref col_ink <- clrs$palette$ink col_muted <- clrs$palette$muted col_outline <- clrs$palette$outline col_bg <- clrs$background ### |- titles and caption ---- title_text <- "Cholesterol's link to death looks different at different ages" subtitle_text <- glue( "Each tile compares the death rate of US adults in one cholesterol group with adults at 180–199 mg/dL (1.00).
", "{sprintf('%.2f', crude_240$value)} means a {pct_crude}% higher death rate; ", "{sprintf('%.2f', dip$value)} means {pct_dip}% lower." ) cue_crude <- glue( "Average age in this group: {round(age_240)},\nagainst {round(age_ref)} in the comparison group" ) note_adj <- "Taking age and sex into account,\nthe highest group no longer stands out" note_young <- glue( "Based on {young_240$deaths} deaths. Without survey\n", "weights, the interval includes 1.00:\n", "{sprintf('%.2f', young_unw$value)} ({sprintf('%.2f', young_unw$lo)}–{sprintf('%.2f', young_unw$hi)})" ) note_low <- "Low cholesterol is associated with higher mortality here;\ntreatment and underlying illness are not measured." ## three caption lines caption_lines <- c( "Hazard ratios with 95% intervals, survey-weighted Cox models (CDC 20-year exam weights) stratified by NHANES cycle; rows 2–5 adjusted for age and sex.", glue( "{comma(n_adults)} adults, {comma(n_deaths)} deaths, follow-up through 2019; HDL over 140 mg/dL excluded. ", "Colour marks intervals entirely above or below 1.00." ), "Observational: statin use, smoking and illness at the exam are not measured; the pattern does not show what changing cholesterol would do." ) caption_text <- paste0( caption_lines[1], "
", caption_lines[2], "
", caption_lines[3], "
", create_social_caption( tt_year = 2026, tt_week = 46, source_text = "NHANES 1999–2018 and NCHS Linked Mortality Files via TidyTuesday" ) ) ### |- plot theme ---- base_theme <- create_base_theme(clrs) weekly_theme <- extend_weekly_theme( base_theme, theme( plot.title = element_textbox_simple( face = "bold", family = title_family, size = title_size, color = col_ink, lineheight = 1.0, margin = margin(b = 10) ), plot.subtitle = element_textbox_simple( family = fonts$subtitle, size = 11, color = col_ink, lineheight = 1.3, margin = margin(b = 6) ), plot.caption = element_textbox_simple( family = fonts$caption, size = 6.6, color = col_muted, lineheight = 1.35, margin = margin(t = 8) ), legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", legend.location = "plot", legend.title = element_blank(), legend.text = element_text(family = fonts$text, size = 8.5, color = col_muted), legend.key.size = unit(0.42, "cm"), legend.margin = margin(t = 2, b = 0), axis.text = element_blank(), axis.title = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(14, 20, 8, 20) ) ) theme_set(weekly_theme) ``` ```` ::: #### [6. Plot]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: plot #| warning: false ### |- matrix ---- tile_w <- 0.94 tile_h <- 0.86 x_lab <- 0.42 x_note <- 6.62 row_labels <- tibble( y = unname(row_y), main = c("(1) All adults", "(2) All adults", "Ages 18–49", "Ages 50–69", "Ages 70+"), sub = c("before taking age and sex into account", "taking age and sex into account", "", "", "") ) ### |- main plot ---- p <- ggplot(cells) + # Geoms geom_tile(aes(x = col, y = y, fill = status), width = tile_w, height = tile_h, color = NA) + geom_tile( data = filter(cells, status %in% c("unclear", "ref")), aes(x = col, y = y), width = tile_w, height = tile_h, fill = NA, color = col_outline, linewidth = 0.3 ) + geom_text( aes( x = col, y = y_hr, label = lab_hr, color = if_else(status %in% c("higher", "lower"), "on_dark", "on_light") ), family = fonts$text, fontface = "bold", size = 4.1 ) + geom_text( aes( x = col, y = y - 0.19, label = lab_ci, color = if_else(status %in% c("higher", "lower"), "on_dark", "on_light") ), family = fonts$caption, size = 2.5 ) + # column headers annotate("text", x = 1:6, y = 7.4, label = bins_show, family = fonts$text, fontface = "bold", size = 3.3, color = col_ink ) + annotate("text", x = 0.53, y = 7.85, hjust = 0, label = "Total cholesterol, mg/dL", family = fonts$text, size = 3.1, color = col_muted ) + # row labels geom_text( data = row_labels, aes(x = x_lab, y = y + if_else(sub == "", 0, 0.12), label = main), hjust = 1, family = fonts$text, fontface = "bold", size = 3.3, color = col_ink ) + geom_text( data = filter(row_labels, sub != ""), aes(x = x_lab, y = y - 0.2, label = sub), hjust = 1, family = fonts$text, size = 2.9, color = col_muted ) + annotate("text", x = x_lab, y = 4.18, hjust = 1, label = "(3) By age group", family = fonts$text, fontface = "bold", size = 3.3, color = col_ink ) + annotate("text", x = x_lab, y = 3.85, hjust = 1, label = "taking age and sex into account", family = fonts$text, size = 2.9, color = col_muted ) + # context row: mean age (subordinate) annotate("text", x = 1:6, y = 6.95, label = round(mean_age$value), family = fonts$caption, size = 3, color = col_muted ) + annotate("text", x = x_lab, y = 6.95, hjust = 1, label = "Average age", family = fonts$text, size = 2.9, color = col_muted ) + # notes at the mark: one per step on the right, the low-end caveat below annotate("text", x = x_note, y = row_y[["crude_all"]], hjust = 0, label = cue_crude, family = fonts$text, size = 2.8, color = col_ink, lineheight = 1.15 ) + annotate("text", x = x_note, y = row_y[["adj_all"]], hjust = 0, label = note_adj, family = fonts$text, size = 2.8, color = col_ink, lineheight = 1.15 ) + annotate("text", x = x_note, y = row_y[["adj_18_49"]], hjust = 0, label = note_young, family = fonts$text, size = 2.8, color = col_ink, lineheight = 1.15 ) + annotate("segment", x = 1 - tile_w / 2, xend = 1 + tile_w / 2, y = 0.73, yend = 0.73, color = col_ink, linewidth = 0.4 ) + annotate("text", x = 1 - tile_w / 2, y = 0.61, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, label = note_low, family = fonts$text, size = 2.8, color = col_ink, lineheight = 1.15 ) + # Scales scale_fill_manual( values = c(higher = col_higher, lower = col_lower, unclear = col_unclear, ref = col_ref), breaks = c("higher", "lower", "unclear"), labels = c("Higher death rate", "Lower death rate", "No clear difference") ) + scale_color_manual(values = c(on_dark = "#FFFFFF", on_light = col_ink), guide = "none") + guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = col_outline, linewidth = 0.3))) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-2.6, 9.6), expand = expansion(0)) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.15, 8.05), expand = expansion(0)) + # Labs labs(title = title_text, subtitle = subtitle_text, caption = caption_text) ``` ```` ::: ### [7.
